Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/10/Text/9] Variables in Model B explained a large amount of variance in T2 well-being indices—49.0% for self-esteem, 29.5% for positive affect, and 65.3% for disordered eating (Cohen, 1988).

sample_type.evidence_source: [/page/10/Table/7] Because our participants ranged in age from 10−18 years, one reviewer suggested running an analysis with age as a control variable instead of physical maturity. We ran Model A with T1 age in place of physical maturity. Similar to the analysis with physical maturity, mastery/autonomy-support and performance climate were positive predictors of perceived competence and were the only two significant paths in the model (aside from the autocorrelations). The model showed a reasonable but worse fit to the data, \chi^2(261) = 455.13, p < .05 (\chi^2/df = 1.74); RMSEA = .07 (90% CI = .055–.075); CFI = .91; GFI = .84. Thus, we retained physical maturity in Model A as the control variable.
